tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

1	# Rig card — VTI
2	
3	*Rig-level machine facts for the Sharpe Lab VTI (variable-temperature
4	insert) cryostat. Canonical copy: `hera/rig-cards/VTI.md` in the
5	`measurement-env` repo; deployed as `rig_card.md` next to
6	`device_card.md` in the measurement directory. Errors or gaps found
7	in-session go to `session_notes.md`, not this file — agents are
8	read-only on the repo.*
9	
10	## Identity
11	- **Rig**: VTI — wet variable-temperature insert (closed-loop He
12	  recirculation), out-of-plane magnet
13	- **Rig owner**: Bingcheng (VTI czar) — adjudicates envelope and
14	  operating-edge questions
15	- **Control PC**: `dgg-vti` (Windows 11); measurement dirs under
16	  `~/VTI_local_data/<user>/<session>/`
17	- **Base temperature**: ≈ 1.2–1.3 K; electron temperature ≈ 8 K
18	- **Status**: in service
19	
20	## Magnet
21	
22	- **Supply / driver**: CAEN ELS FAST-PS 1K5, `drivers.FastBi1K5`
23	  (raw TCP `192.168.0.10:10001`). Out-of-plane field, Tesla, via the
24	  `field` qcodes Parameter.
25	- **Coil constant**: `T_per_A = 1/7.3` ≈ 0.137 T/A.
26	- **Ramp rate**: fixed 1 A/min ≈ **0.137 T/min**, hard-coded in the
27	  driver and sent with every setpoint. An 8 T traverse is a ~58 min
28	  floor.
29	- **Set semantics**: `magnet.field(target)` **blocks** until the field
30	  is reached (polls the ramping flag, then a `settle_s` dwell — default
31	  3 s, tunable). A cell that ramps is busy the whole ramp.
32	- **Interrupt ≠ stop**: interrupting the notebook cell does **not**
33	  stop the supply — it keeps ramping to the last setpoint. There is no
34	  abort/pause/ramp-to-zero method; recovery is calling `field()` again
35	  with a new target. Aborting a ramp is the operator acting on the
36	  instrument, never a kernel interrupt.
37	- **Magnet limit**: **14.0 T** (Zack ruling 2026-06-12), enforced by
38	  the driver (`max_field_T = 14.0`; ramping above it raises). The
39	  session cap (device card / SAFETIES, machine-enforced via
40	  `magnet.field.vals`) is what measurements obey.
41	- **High field + elevated T interact through the probe's coupling to
42	  the bath**; not expected to bite below ~100 K (heuristic — Aaron,
43	  2026-08-02, bath-vs-probe-T response unmeasured).
44	- **Read-truth**: `field()`'s get returns the **measured** output
45	  current × `T_per_A` (`GET:I:?`, 2-stage moving-average readback,
46	  ~41 ms lag ≈ 0.1 mT at our slew). The set-point is not readable as
47	  field; never infer field from the last set call.
48	- **Persistent switch / output**: heater `heater_on()` / `heater_off()`
49	  (each blocks 10 s, **no field-matching check** — operator-only);
50	  state reads `magnet.persistent_switch_on()`, `magnet.output_enabled()`.
51	- **Never re-traverse**: the fixed slow ramp makes field the expensive
52	  axis. Plan sweeps to start where the magnet sits and end where the
53	  next measurement needs it; alternate fan directions across
54	  iterations rather than returning to a preferred start field.
55	
56	## Thermometry & heaters
57	
58	- **Controller**: Lakeshore 335 (`drivers.Lakeshore_335`).
59	  Input A = sample-mount Cernox (`sample_temperature`, `KRDG? A`);
60	  input B = vaporizer Cernox (`vaporizer_temperature`, `KRDG? B`).
61	- **Readout is file-based, never GPIB**: the lakeshore worker (VTI
62	  Monitor launcher) owns LS335 polling and writes InfluxDB (`vti`) plus
63	  `C:\Users\DGG\temperature_logs\VTI_{sample,vaporizer}.txt`. Logfile
64	  cadence **5 s** (InfluxDB 30 s; worker `READ_INTERVAL`, 2026-07-16).
65	  Freshness guards must allow **≥ 2–3 write periods** — a threshold
66	  equal to the cadence false-fires at end-of-period (burned: ladder v2,
67	  2026-07-15). The kernel
68	  reads `T_sample` / `T_vaporizer` via
69	  `temperature_from_logfiles(VTI.temp_logfile_candidates[...])`,
70	  `fp()`-able as recorded channels; the `heater` instance is control-only
71	  (setpoints / ranges / power). A frozen logfile (dead worker) reads a
72	  plausible value that `assert T < base` cannot catch — at bring-up
73	  confirm the logfile mtime is advancing.
74	- **Sensors**: 2× CX-1030-CU-HT-0.3M (serials X225149, X225150),
75	  NIST-traceable ITS-90, 0.3–420 K. Calibration packages in-repo at
76	  `hera/vti/cernox-cal/` (INDEX.md has the error budget). Curve
77	  assignments (read from NVRAM 2026-06-12): **input A = curve 23,
78	  serial X225149**; input B = curve 21, whose header *also* reads
79	  X225149 — likely X225150's data loaded under an unedited name, or a
80	  duplicate load of A's curve. Impact is bounded by the inter-sensor
81	  cal delta and B is control-only, but the anomaly is unresolved
82	  (Bingcheng).
83	- **Accuracy**: ±6–9 mK at 10–20 K, zero-field. Field-induced error:
84	  order tens of mK at 10 K / 6 T (CX-1030 magnetoresistance runs a
85	  few× the published CX-1050 table), negligible above ~30 K. B is
86	  logged per point, so the field term is a clean post-hoc correction.
87	- **Control topology**: both LS335 loops are closed-loop (loop 1
88	  sample-mount heater ↔ input A; loop 2 vaporizer ↔ input B). The
89	  sanctioned elevated-T method is **`heater.set_both(T, ratio=0.95)`**,
90	  authorized **≤ 100 K** (Aaron, 2026-07-18, via Zack). The **needle
91	  valve remains operator-only, hands at the rig**.
92	- **Sample-loop PID is untuned** (confirmed live 2026-07-15): upward
93	  setpoint steps overshoot **~+1.4 K**, and recovery is bath-limited —
94	  the sample cools only toward the vaporizer floor at `ratio·T`, so
95	  the overshoot penalty scales with (1 − ratio). At ratio 0.99:
96	  ~0.015 K/min recovery; tolerance-settling never passed below ~20 K.
97	  Accept elevated-T points on *stability*, not proximity (hover
98	  acceptance — temperature-dependence VTI variant). Tuning backlogged
99	  (eng-backlog, Bingcheng).
100	- **Offsets**: the mount→device thermal gradient is **uncharacterized**
101	  (heater-power dependent). Treat absolute-T claims accordingly; LK
102	  fits inherit T errors linearly. Ask the operator.
103	
104	
105	## Silent preconditions
106	
107	Per the prompt's "preflight the silent preconditions" working-style
108	bullet — state sweeps depend on but never set, with the cheap read for
109	each. (LS335 control instance is named `heater`; temperature is read from
110	the worker logfiles via `T_sample` / `T_vaporizer`.)
111	
112	| Hazard | One-line read | Expected at rest | Why silent |
113	|---|---|---|---|
114	| Sample temperature | `T_sample()` | ≈ 1.2–1.3 K at base | every sweep assumes T; almost none set it |
115	| Magnet field | `magnet.field()` (measured readback) | wherever the last ramp ended — read, never assume 0 | gate sweeps inherit B from prior cells |
116	| Vaporizer state | `T_vaporizer()` | tracks base unless a ladder is in progress | needle-valve setting is manual and persists across cells |
117	| PS heater / output | `magnet.persistent_switch_on()`, `magnet.output_enabled()` | heater on, output enabled (`field()` raises otherwise) | touched only at bring-up |
118	
119	## Sweep stack & data layout
120	
121	The `sweep` package (measureme submodule) is the single source of truth for the
122	station/sweep call surface, the on-disk run format, and the metadata schema:
123	`docs/api/measureme.md`. Stations are built with `sweep.AsyncStation`. Rig
124	specifics:
125	
126	- **Measurement dir**: each sweep writes `<measurement_dir>/data/<file_id>/`,
127	  the measurement dir being `~/VTI_local_data/<user>/<session>/`.
128	- **`plot.png` is the live monitor, not the measurement** — for rastered /
129	  co-swept maps it does not show the physical map; re-form from the TSV before
130	  any visual read.
131	- **Mixed metadata on disk**: this rig's corpus spans both schema versions
132	  (older singular keys; current plural + `version`/`instruments`). Load through
133	  `hera.analysis` / `sweep.sweep_load`, never hand-rolled.
134	
135	## Timing rules of thumb
136	
137	Defaults for wall-clock arithmetic — calibrate against runs in the
138	current measurement dir before pricing anything long, and cite the
139	calibrating run.
140	
141	- **Per-point ≈ dwell + readback.** Instrument reads serialize:
142	  ~25–30 ms per read, SR830 X+P batching into one SNAP?. Standard fp
143	  set ≈ **0.2–0.25 s/pt** at NPLC=1 (20260714.2 run 4; 2026-06-14
144	  fan); ~1.1 s/pt with the 2400s at NPLC=10 (pA-floor gate-current
145	  reads, typical until early leakage checks are done — 20260714.2
146	  runs 0–3). Include NPLC when recording a timing calibration.
147	- **Gatemap row turnaround ≈ flyback**: the fast axis steps home at
148	  `volt.step`, ~6 ms/write — span/`volt.step` × 6 ms + slow_delay
149	  (run 4: 6 V at 5 mV + slow_delay=3 → 12 s/row); scales with the
150	  fast span. Fan wall-clock ÷ points (~2.1 s/pt, run 7) folds ramps +
151	  turnaround in — not a per-point rate.
152	- **Fan arithmetic**: wall-clock ≈ B_span / 0.137 T/min (ramp floor)
153	  + N_rows × (N_fast × per-point + row turnaround).
154	- **Row turnaround**: ~60 s/row at fine B steps (run 5, 2026-06-10:
155	  121 rows × 271 pts, predicted 12.3 h vs actual 13.6 h). At coarse
156	  steps rows are ramp-limited instead (run 3: 278 s/row at 0.25 T
157	  steps ≈ 110 s ramp + turnaround).
158	- **Measured ramps are slower than bare ramps**: a field traverse
159	  recorded as a sweep moves at ~0.092 T/min effective (per-point
160	  overhead on top of the 0.137 bare rate) — ~40% more wall-clock than
161	  an unrecorded ramp. Usually still worth it; price honestly.
162	- **Closed-loop T settles run 2–5 min** on this rig (2026-06-10/12
163	  ladder, ~54 min/pt dominated by sweeps) — not the 10–20 min of
164	  toploader lore. Don't inherit settle budgets across rigs. Up-leg
165	  catches 2.5–4 min (2026-07-15 ladder); descents are
166	  passive-cooling-limited (τ ≈ 27 min measured 34→25 K at ratio 0.99)
167	  — see the temperature-dependence VTI variant's descend-catch pattern.
168	
169	## Standard equipment
170	
171	Racked inventory with defaults; anything marked **(per-device)** is a
172	hole the device card fills, and the device card wins any conflict.
173	
174	- **Lock-ins**: SR830 family, 4 in recent service (`sr0…sr3`). Channel
175	  roles, gains, sensitivities, contact pairs: (per-device).
176	  **Settling**: `time_constant` + `filter_slope` are operator-set on the
177	  front panel and **not set by the kit** — read them (`srN.time_constant()`,
178	  `srN.filter_slope()`) at bring-up and record them, so the swept-point dwell
179	  (`≳ k·τ`; k ≈ 5 at 6 dB/oct, 7–10 at 24 dB/oct) can be priced against a
180	  known τ and bent knowingly, not guessed (STYLE rule 12 settling floor). The
181	  run-metadata `instruments` snapshot currently stores these as `None` —
182	  until that's fixed, the bring-up record is the only place τ lives on disk.
183	- **Current preamp**: Ithaco transimpedance preamp on the drain
184	  channel; gain setting (per-device), recorded per run in
185	  `measurement_config`.
186	- **DC sources**: SRS DC205 (serial, 115200 baud, **ASRL7**,
187	  s/n 20500514) — use `drivers.SRS_DC205` (rate-based ramp,
188	  deterministic dV/dt); the
189	  `sharpelab_nb` driver of the same name has different ramp semantics
190	  and they are **not interchangeable**. 2× Keithley 2400 for gates.
191	  The Keithley `volt.step`, the DC205 `ramp_rate`, and `inter_delay` are
192	  operator-owned — the agent never changes them.
193	- **Contact mux**: QDevil QSwitch (expected IDN: serial 37, firmware
194	  2.0) via `drivers.QSwitch` + `drivers.contact_mux.ContactMux`.
195	  **Max signal voltage 60 V DC** (30 Vrms / 42 Vpp AC) — QDevil's rated
196	  limit (`docs/manuals/qswitch/`, §3.1 + specifications table); every
197	  signal line routed through the switch must stay within it.
198	  USB-CDC serial (Microchip VID_04D8), **ASRL4**.
199	  Switching grounds lines during transitions; `settle_s` default 10 s
200	  (read `mux.settle_s`).
201	  Per-cooldown bless status (validated address, any `settle_s` override)
202	  lives in the device card; `ContactMux` is live only when the device
203	  card says so. The `lines`/`breakouts` maps are wiring → (per-device).
204	- **Terranova 906A gauge**: serial, **ASRL8** — held by the
205	  influx-logger kernel.
206	- **He level**: AMI Model 1700 (`drivers.AMI_1700`),
207	  `192.168.0.100:7180` (s/n 1700-20-207).
208	- **Instrument LAN** (isolated 192.168.0/24): `.10` FastBi supply,
209	  `.100` AMI 1700, `.101` this PC, `.1` router.
210	
211	## Known quirks
212	
213	- Console is cp1252; `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` is set in `~/.bashrc`
214	  to address unicode issues.
215	
216	## What this card does not carry
217	
218	- **Device facts** — wiring/contact maps, gains, gate stacks,
219	  validators, calibrated settle times → device card.
220	- **Campaign state** — goals, recipes in play, reference runs → brief.
221	- **Session caps** — field/T/voltage limits chosen for a session →
222	  device card + SAFETIES cell.
223	- **Conclusions** — no prior-campaign operating points, no device
224	  leans, no "last time X worked". This card is agent-visible during
225	  blinded sessions, and operational defaults are also information.
226

- **Readout is file-based, never GPIB**: the lakeshore worker (VTI
  Monitor launcher) owns LS335 polling and writes InfluxDB (`vti`) plus
  `C:\Users\DGG\temperature_logs\VTI_{sample,vaporizer}.txt`. Logfile
  cadence **5 s** (InfluxDB 30 s; worker `READ_INTERVAL`, 2026-07-16).
  Freshness guards must allow **≥ 2–3 write periods** — a threshold
  equal to the cadence false-fires at end-of-period (burned: ladder v2,
  2026-07-15). The kernel
  reads `T_sample` / `T_vaporizer` via
  `temperature_from_logfiles(VTI.temp_logfile_candidates[...])`,
  `fp()`-able as recorded channels; the `heater` instance is control-only
  (setpoints / ranges / power). A frozen logfile (dead worker) reads a
  plausible value that `assert T < base` cannot catch — at bring-up
  confirm the logfile mtime is advancing.
- **Sensors**: 2× CX-1030-CU-HT-0.3M (serials X225149, X225150),
  NIST-traceable ITS-90, 0.3–420 K. Calibration packages in-repo at
  `hera/vti/cernox-cal/` (INDEX.md has the error budget). Curve
  assignments (read from NVRAM 2026-06-12): **input A = curve 23,
  serial X225149**; input B = curve 21, whose header *also* reads
  X225149 — likely X225150's data loaded under an unedited name, or a
  duplicate load of A's curve. Impact is bounded by the inter-sensor
  cal delta and B is control-only, but the anomaly is unresolved
  (Bingcheng).
- **Accuracy**: ±6–9 mK at 10–20 K, zero-field. Field-induced error:
  order tens of mK at 10 K / 6 T (CX-1030 magnetoresistance runs a
  few× the published CX-1050 table), negligible above ~30 K. B is
  logged per point, so the field term is a clean post-hoc correction.
- **Control topology**: both LS335 loops are closed-loop (loop 1
  sample-mount heater ↔ input A; loop 2 vaporizer ↔ input B). The
  sanctioned elevated-T method is **`heater.set_both(T, ratio=0.95)`**,
  authorized **≤ 100 K** (Aaron, 2026-07-18, via Zack). The **needle
  valve remains operator-only, hands at the rig**.
- **Sample-loop PID is untuned** (confirmed live 2026-07-15): upward
  setpoint steps overshoot **~+1.4 K**, and recovery is bath-limited —
  the sample cools only toward the vaporizer floor at `ratio·T`, so
  the overshoot penalty scales with (1 − ratio). At ratio 0.99:
  ~0.015 K/min recovery; tolerance-settling never passed below ~20 K.
  Accept elevated-T points on *stability*, not proximity (hover
  acceptance — temperature-dependence VTI variant). Tuning backlogged
  (eng-backlog, Bingcheng).
- **Offsets**: the mount→device thermal gradient is **uncharacterized**
  (heater-power dependent). Treat absolute-T claims accordingly; LK
  fits inherit T errors linearly. Ask the operator.


## Silent preconditions

Per the prompt's "preflight the silent preconditions" working-style
bullet — state sweeps depend on but never set, with the cheap read for
each. (LS335 control instance is named `heater`; temperature is read from
the worker logfiles via `T_sample` / `T_vaporizer`.)

| Hazard | One-line read | Expected at rest | Why silent |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sample temperature | `T_sample()` | ≈ 1.2–1.3 K at base | every sweep assumes T; almost none set it |
| Magnet field | `magnet.field()` (measured readback) | wherever the last ramp ended — read, never assume 0 | gate sweeps inherit B from prior cells |
| Vaporizer state | `T_vaporizer()` | tracks base unless a ladder is in progress | needle-valve setting is manual and persists across cells |
| PS heater / output | `magnet.persistent_switch_on()`, `magnet.output_enabled()` | heater on, output enabled (`field()` raises otherwise) | touched only at bring-up |

## Sweep stack & data layout

The `sweep` package (measureme submodule) is the single source of truth for the
station/sweep call surface, the on-disk run format, and the metadata schema:
`docs/api/measureme.md`. Stations are built with `sweep.AsyncStation`. Rig
specifics:

- **Measurement dir**: each sweep writes `<measurement_dir>/data/<file_id>/`,
  the measurement dir being `~/VTI_local_data/<user>/<session>/`.
- **`plot.png` is the live monitor, not the measurement** — for rastered /
  co-swept maps it does not show the physical map; re-form from the TSV before
  any visual read.
- **Mixed metadata on disk**: this rig's corpus spans both schema versions
  (older singular keys; current plural + `version`/`instruments`). Load through
  `hera.analysis` / `sweep.sweep_load`, never hand-rolled.

## Timing rules of thumb

Defaults for wall-clock arithmetic — calibrate against runs in the
current measurement dir before pricing anything long, and cite the
calibrating run.

- **Per-point ≈ dwell + readback.** Instrument reads serialize:
  ~25–30 ms per read, SR830 X+P batching into one SNAP?. Standard fp
  set ≈ **0.2–0.25 s/pt** at NPLC=1 (20260714.2 run 4; 2026-06-14
  fan); ~1.1 s/pt with the 2400s at NPLC=10 (pA-floor gate-current
  reads, typical until early leakage checks are done — 20260714.2
  runs 0–3). Include NPLC when recording a timing calibration.
- **Gatemap row turnaround ≈ flyback**: the fast axis steps home at
  `volt.step`, ~6 ms/write — span/`volt.step` × 6 ms + slow_delay
  (run 4: 6 V at 5 mV + slow_delay=3 → 12 s/row); scales with the
  fast span. Fan wall-clock ÷ points (~2.1 s/pt, run 7) folds ramps +
  turnaround in — not a per-point rate.
- **Fan arithmetic**: wall-clock ≈ B_span / 0.137 T/min (ramp floor)
  + N_rows × (N_fast × per-point + row turnaround).
- **Row turnaround**: ~60 s/row at fine B steps (run 5, 2026-06-10:
  121 rows × 271 pts, predicted 12.3 h vs actual 13.6 h). At coarse
  steps rows are ramp-limited instead (run 3: 278 s/row at 0.25 T
  steps ≈ 110 s ramp + turnaround).
- **Measured ramps are slower than bare ramps**: a field traverse
  recorded as a sweep moves at ~0.092 T/min effective (per-point
  overhead on top of the 0.137 bare rate) — ~40% more wall-clock than
  an unrecorded ramp. Usually still worth it; price honestly.
- **Closed-loop T settles run 2–5 min** on this rig (2026-06-10/12
  ladder, ~54 min/pt dominated by sweeps) — not the 10–20 min of
  toploader lore. Don't inherit settle budgets across rigs. Up-leg
  catches 2.5–4 min (2026-07-15 ladder); descents are
  passive-cooling-limited (τ ≈ 27 min measured 34→25 K at ratio 0.99)
  — see the temperature-dependence VTI variant's descend-catch pattern.

## Standard equipment

Racked inventory with defaults; anything marked **(per-device)** is a
hole the device card fills, and the device card wins any conflict.

- **Lock-ins**: SR830 family, 4 in recent service (`sr0…sr3`). Channel
  roles, gains, sensitivities, contact pairs: (per-device).
  **Settling**: `time_constant` + `filter_slope` are operator-set on the
  front panel and **not set by the kit** — read them (`srN.time_constant()`,
  `srN.filter_slope()`) at bring-up and record them, so the swept-point dwell
  (`≳ k·τ`; k ≈ 5 at 6 dB/oct, 7–10 at 24 dB/oct) can be priced against a
  known τ and bent knowingly, not guessed (STYLE rule 12 settling floor). The
  run-metadata `instruments` snapshot currently stores these as `None` —
  until that's fixed, the bring-up record is the only place τ lives on disk.
- **Current preamp**: Ithaco transimpedance preamp on the drain
  channel; gain setting (per-device), recorded per run in
  `measurement_config`.
- **DC sources**: SRS DC205 (serial, 115200 baud, **ASRL7**,
  s/n 20500514) — use `drivers.SRS_DC205` (rate-based ramp,
  deterministic dV/dt); the
  `sharpelab_nb` driver of the same name has different ramp semantics
  and they are **not interchangeable**. 2× Keithley 2400 for gates.
  The Keithley `volt.step`, the DC205 `ramp_rate`, and `inter_delay` are
  operator-owned — the agent never changes them.
- **Contact mux**: QDevil QSwitch (expected IDN: serial 37, firmware
  2.0) via `drivers.QSwitch` + `drivers.contact_mux.ContactMux`.
  **Max signal voltage 60 V DC** (30 Vrms / 42 Vpp AC) — QDevil's rated
  limit (`docs/manuals/qswitch/`, §3.1 + specifications table); every
  signal line routed through the switch must stay within it.
  USB-CDC serial (Microchip VID_04D8), **ASRL4**.
  Switching grounds lines during transitions; `settle_s` default 10 s
  (read `mux.settle_s`).
  Per-cooldown bless status (validated address, any `settle_s` override)
  lives in the device card; `ContactMux` is live only when the device
  card says so. The `lines`/`breakouts` maps are wiring → (per-device).
- **Terranova 906A gauge**: serial, **ASRL8** — held by the
  influx-logger kernel.
- **He level**: AMI Model 1700 (`drivers.AMI_1700`),
  `192.168.0.100:7180` (s/n 1700-20-207).
- **Instrument LAN** (isolated 192.168.0/24): `.10` FastBi supply,
  `.100` AMI 1700, `.101` this PC, `.1` router.

## Known quirks

- Console is cp1252; `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` is set in `~/.bashrc`
  to address unicode issues.

## What this card does not carry

- **Device facts** — wiring/contact maps, gains, gate stacks,
  validators, calibrated settle times → device card.
- **Campaign state** — goals, recipes in play, reference runs → brief.
- **Session caps** — field/T/voltage limits chosen for a session →
  device card + SAFETIES cell.
- **Conclusions** — no prior-campaign operating points, no device
  leans, no "last time X worked". This card is agent-visible during
  blinded sessions, and operational defaults are also information.

Sensitivity fixed at 50 µV (5 kΩ FS): R(B = 0) ≈ 70 Ω is 1.4 % of range, but there is no SdH below ~1.5 T and the MR + SdH maxima at high B need the headroom; the FFT window starts above onset. **Price:** 10 T bare traverse 73 min + 921 × ~3.8 s per-point overhead (settle 3 s + reads) ≈ 58 min → **≈ 2 h 15 m**, ending at **10 T with the gates at the spot** — the hole-side spot check (n = −1.2×10¹²) then rides the magnet down 10 → 0.3 T, never re-traversing. Checkpoints: first 20 points (signal, sensitivity, leakage, field readback tracking setpoints); at ~3 T and ~6 T a partial FFT on the landed record (onset, tone count) — abort if the channel rails or no oscillation content has appeared by 6 T with R flat (then the fan is pointless at this T_e and the read is resolution-limited).

1	# Landau fan
2	
3	## What
4	2D map of carrier density × magnetic field at fixed displacement field: `mag.field` as the **slow** axis of a `multimegasweep`, with a paired-(k_tg, k_bg) n-line (fixed D, via `calculate_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, dtg=..., dbg=...)`) as the **fast** axis:
5	```python
6	s.multimegasweep([mag.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=1, fast_delay=0.9)
7	```
8	Field is slow because gates are cheap to retrace and the magnet is not — the magnet ramps once, monotonically, across the whole fan. Every lock-in X/P read at each grid point. Analysis side plots B vs n (`pcolormesh`) per contact pair and overlays Středa lines (see Verify). Distinct from its two neighbors: `field-sweep-1d` is one gate point with full B-axis density; `gatemap-in-field` is the full 2D gate plane at a *single* B. The fan trades both for the (n, B) plane — the only measurement that resolves how gapped states *disperse* with field.
9	
10	## When
11	Three triggers, in rough campaign order:
12	- **Oscillation check** — a `field-sweep-1d` or `gatemap-in-field` showed quantum-oscillation-like wiggles and you need to know if they're real. The corpus idiom is literally named for this: RPL_19's "Small fan to check if oscillations are real" (a 161 × 151 fan after an effective-mass series kept hinting at SdH). A feature that moves systematically across the n-line as B steps is physics; one that doesn't is noise or gate drift.
13	- **State classification** — a map shows a vanishing-ρxx region (or a busy set of dips) and the discriminating question is whether the features disperse. This is the classification backbone of an FQAH/SC-style campaign (arXiv 2504.06972: ρxx(ν_h, B) fans + Středa fits are how (R/F/I)QAH states were separated from the SC region).
14	- **Calibration** — SdH/LL frequency vs n gives cap ratios independently of the CNP-slope method, and for a moiré device the fan anchors the moiré density n_M. The extraction is `cap-ratio-calibration`'s job (deferred — recipe not yet written); the fan is its input data.
15	
16	Prerequisites are `nD-map`'s plus a field-verified magnet: cap ratios `dtg`/`dbg` must be trusted (the fast axis is a line in (n, D) — wrong caps tilt it), and the field source must be live (Yokogawa cache seeded after kernel restart, AMI430 in operating mode — see `field-sweep-1d` plumbing notes).
17	
18	## Why
19	A dip in ρxx at one B value is ambiguous — gap, SC, contact artifact, density wobble. The same dip tracked across a fan is nearly unambiguous: a gapped state at fixed filling traces a straight line in (n, B) whose slope *is* its Chern number (Středa: dn/dB = C·e/h), an SC pocket sits at fixed n and dies at moderate B without dispersing, and quantum oscillations fan out with 1/B periodicity that yields the Fermi-surface area. One measurement, three discriminations, plus calibration for free.
20	
21	The cost is real: these are the most expensive sweeps in the corpus. Reference wall-clocks *(our-measurement, toploader, non-blocking-magnet era — the formula below them omits the traverse term; do not carry these numbers to another rig untagged)*: RPL_10's 101 B × 101 n fan at `slow_delay=30, fast_delay=1` took **4.3 h** (file 156); the 351 × 251 version took **27.8 h** (file 159); RPL_19's 161 × 151 at `fast_delay=0.6` took **5.5 h** (file 1776 — Aaron's own `# 1776, took 5.5 hours` annotation propagates through later fan cells); the 441 × 231 fan to 5 T took **30.1 h** (file 1840). Aaron's inline arithmetic (`(351*501)/(201*151)*3` in 20260124 cell 134) is the toploader-era form.
22	
23	**Estimate before you run — the full cost model**: wall-clock = **field-traverse time + N_rows × (row turnaround + N_fast × per-point time)**. Which term dominates is a rig property, not a constant of nature: **if the field source is ramp-rate-limited and the set call blocks** (check the rig card for whether yours is), the traverse term is fixed by the B-span alone — **finer B steps cost only row turnaround, and coarsening B buys aliasing, not time**. Traverses come in two species, priced differently: a **bare ramp** moves at the magnet's ramp rate; a **measured traverse** (the same leg recorded as a sweep) moves at an effective rate degraded by per-point overhead. A "free" measured ramp-down is usually still worth taking — it buys data for wall-clock — but it is not free: price it at the measured rate, from the rig card's Timing rules (`rig_card.md`), never the bare one. Calibrate row turnaround and per-point time from this session's own first sweeps; inherited timing constants carry a provenance tag and the conditions they were measured under, or they are guesses.
24	
25	## Recipe
26	1. Pick the n-window and fixed D from the map that motivated the fan, and decide the B span. Corpus shapes: oscillation check 0.9 → 2.5 T over a 151-pt n-line; classification fan 0 → 2.5 T, 251 × 151; deep fan 0.6 → 5 T, 441 × 231; high-field 5 → 12 T, 351 × 201. Start coarse (≤200 B steps, ≤151 n points); zoom only on confirmed structure. **Grid Nyquist check, both axes, at design time**: against the finest expected feature spacing in the analysis window. The **B-axis** check depends on the read: a **Středa/SC fan** (dip positions, no FFT) samples uniform in B, may start at 0, and needs ≥2 (prefer 3) rows per LL period ΔB ≈ (g·e/h)·B²/n (g = 4 for spin×valley) at the **lowest-B, highest-n corner**; a **per-column SdH-FFT fan** samples uniform in 1/B (`field_invB`, B_lo > 0) and needs Δ(1/B) ≤ 1/(2·F) (prefer 1/3) at the highest n, F = (h/4e)·n. The **n-axis** check (both): ray spacing Δn = g·(e/h)·B at the lowest B you intend to read, same ≥2 floor. For a **per-column SdH-FFT fan** also compute the resolution **δF = 1/(1/B_onset − 1/B_max)** against the tones the claim must separate (~2·δF to trust a split) — δF is set by the record above onset, not by grid density; if it can't separate the tones, redesign the window or the density, don't densify. An undersampled axis produces in-data aliasing that mimics curved structure and survives re-plotting; no post-hoc check fully recovers it. "Start coarse" applies to the *window*, never below the Nyquist floor of the structure you intend to claim — and where the cost model says fine B is nearly free (blocking ramp-limited magnets), take it. **Re-run this check whenever n_max changes — never inherit the field sampling across fans.** The requirement tightens with n (Δ(1/B) ∝ 1/n, ΔB ∝ B²/n), so a sampling fine enough for an n≤4 fan undersamples an n=10 firming fan (our-measurement, QC0426/VTI 2026-06-14, uniform-B at ΔB=0.1 T: 2.2 rows/period at n=4 but only 1.5 — under the ≥2 floor — at n=10, B=4 T, where a spurious high-n second pocket appeared and had to be killed post-hoc). Where the rig makes fine B *not* free (measurement-dominated fans, e.g. a non-blocking-magnet rig at >1 s/pt — check the cost model), buy the high-n Nyquist floor by **trimming n-points or flooring the high-n claim at B ≥ 5–6 T**, not by coarsening the field sampling. **Dynamic-range check, at design time**: a fan reads through one *fixed* sensitivity, so the scale must clear the **global worst corner**, structurally **low n × high B** — R ∝ 1/n on the gate axis stacks with the B-axis MR (10–100× zero-field). Size full-scale with **headroom, not precision** — saturation is the asymmetric failure: **better to lose low-resistance resolution than saturate** (expert practice). Set the scale comfortably above I_bias·R(n_min, B_max), anchoring R_max from a spot-check/CNP R-anchor × the **low-n** MR factor (MR grows toward CNP; a high-|n| factor under-sizes the corner — our-measurement). **Clipping distorts, it does not drop**: a railed column is flat-topped → harmonics + corrupted bg-subtraction across its whole FFT, unrecoverable by any B-window (the clean data sits at low B, the clip at high B). **Cost-floor check, at design time**: propose **exactly one** fan — the cheapest that clears the two checks above and delivers the claim. Compute `N_B · N_n · t_pt` and set each lever to its floor. **Do not offer a cheaper alternative or defer the trim to the operator — the floored design *is* the proposal.** Levers, in order: (1) **`B_lo` = the measured onset from `hera.analysis.sdh_onset(R, B).onset_b` — compute it, do not eyeball it** (sub-onset rows are background, not signal; a too-low `B_lo` inflates both the 1/B span and the n-axis Nyquist, and eyeballed onsets run systematically too low). If the carrying tone is `censored`, the spot-check record never captured the onset — `onset_b` is that record's low edge, a valid lower bound for `B_lo`; a cheap low-field extension pins it before committing a long fan. `SdhOnsetError` means no usable oscillations — re-examine the spot check, do not guess a `B_lo`; (2) **`n_max` = the validity window of the claim**; (3) `N_n` = its ray-Nyquist floor at `B_lo`; (4) `B_max` = the claim (more periods sharpen tones, but `B_max` past what the claim needs is just cost). `n_max` is the most expensive lever — out-of-validity it pays on *both* `N_B` and `N_n` (`Δ(1/B) ∝ 1/n_max`). State the computed `N_B`, `N_n`, and wall-clock in the proposal.
27	2. Build the fast axis: `ns = np.linspace(n_hi, n_lo, N); Ds = D0 * np.ones(len(ns)); Vtgs, Vbgs = calculate_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, dtg=..., dbg=...)`. A non-uniform n-vector is legitimate when you know where the action is — RPL_19's elevated-T fan stitches `np.hstack((n1, n2, n3))` with the dense segment over the CSC window and coarse segments elsewhere, with `#`-comments labeling each segment (20260124 cell 239).
28	3. Set the sensitivity (from the step-1 dynamic-range check) and time constant as an explicit pre-cell, fixed for the whole fan. RPL_19/20260217 cell 124 is the idiom: `sr830_N.sensitivity(10e-3)`, `sr830_N.time_constant(300e-3)`. Excitation: Aaron runs 1 V (graphene-scale) and bumps to 2.5 V for 12 T work; on a fragile-state device (FQAH/SC, arXiv 2504.06972's 1 nA cap) respect the device-card excitation ceiling instead — the states you're classifying wash out if heated.
29	4. Build the slow field axis: a **per-column SdH-FFT fan** uses `B_vec = field_invB(B_start, B_end, N)` (uniform in 1/B, both > 0); a **Středa/SC fan** uses `np.linspace` and may start at 0. Position the magnet at the fan's start field and let it settle: `s.ramp(mag.field, B_start)` then `time.sleep(600)` for multi-tesla positioning (RPL_19/20260217 cells 88/94), `time.sleep(30)` at ~1 T (RPL_10), `time.sleep(5*60)` at 0.6 T (20260124 cell 235). Plan the direction (endpoint order) so the fan *starts* where the magnet already is and *ends* where the next measurement needs it — never re-traverse. The elevated-T fan covers ±5 T as four chained segments (5→0.6, 0.6→0, 0→−0.6, −0.6→−5; 20260124 cells 239–242), each starting where the last ended.
30	5. Build `s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)`. `s.add_comment('landau-fan')` then a structured tag: `s.add_comment(f'D = {D0} V/nm, n = {n_lo} to {n_hi}, B = {B_start} to {B_end} T')`, plus `s.add_comment(grab_metadata())` where available. **Watch out** — RPL_10's fans carry exemplary comments (`'MC4, Vsi = -20V, quantum oscillations, D = 0.31 V/nm, n = -2.9 to -2.1, B = 1 to 0 T'`); RPL_19's fan cells carry *none* (files 1776/1840 have empty `comments`) — only a stale `# 1776` Python comment. The recipe asks for the RPL_10 discipline.
31	6. `s.ramp(sr830_1.amplitude, A)`, `s.ramp(k_si.volt, V_si)`, `s.ramp(bias_voltage.volt, 0)` if present. `fp` temperature(s) and every lock-in X/P; `plot` gate currents for live leakage (`s.plot(k_bg.volt, k_bg.curr)`, `s.plot('time', k_tg.curr)`, `s.plot('time', k_si.curr)` — RPL_19 fan idiom; note `fp` of gate currents is often omitted here, so leakage lands in the live plot but *not* in the TSV).
32	7. The sweep (step 0 call above). Delay band in the corpus: `slow_delay=1` (gates retrace during it; the field step itself is rate-limited by the magnet), `fast_delay` ≈ 4τ default — a Středa/dispersion fan tolerates the uniform fast-axis lag like a slope; ~6τ when the n-axis carries the extracted signal (per-column SdH FFT, or coarse n), where the lag distorts it, with denser n trading against the dwell.
33	8. Park gates (`k_bg.volt(0); k_tg.volt(0)`), decide the field endpoint deliberately (leave it for a follow-up fan, `s.ramp(mag.field, 0)`, or ride home as a measured traverse — a free `field-sweep-1d`, priced at the measured rate per the Why cost model), and ping (`alerts.discord('🐍jobs done🐍')`) — at 5–30 h these runs outlive operator attention spans.
34	
35	## Verify
36	Disk-side checks, then the Středa read. The fan is unrolled into flat rows; the slow column is `magnet_field`.
37	
38	```python
39	from hera.analysis import open_run, plot_raw, summarize_run
40	import numpy as np
41	
42	run = open_run("<notebook_dir>/data/<file_id>")
43	print(summarize_run(run))
44	# expect: type 2D, recipe 'landau-fan', slow_param ['magnet_field'],
45	#         fast_param ['k_tg_volt', 'k_bg_volt'].
46	
47	# 0. Raw view FIRST — one gain-divided pcolormesh per channel, no log, no
48	#    background removal. Rails/clipping, dead channels, streaks, and row
49	#    jumps are visible here and hidden by every derived (FFT/Středa) view.
50	plot_raw(run)
51	
52	# 1. Completeness — at 5-30 h these are the most interruption-prone sweeps
53	#    in the corpus (RPL_10 file 158 and TD48-era runs died early; Aaron
54	#    re-ran rather than salvaged).
55	assert not run.interrupted, "fan was interrupted; decide re-run vs salvage with the human"
56	
57	# 2. B axis actually traversed the plan, monotonically per segment.
58	B = run.col("magnet_field")
59	print(f"B traversed: {B.min():.3f} → {B.max():.3f} T over {len(run.meta['slow_setpoints'][0])} steps")
60	
61	# 3. Fast axis is a paired n-line: both gate columns move together.
62	vtg, vbg = run.col("k_tg_volt"), run.col("k_bg_volt")
63	assert np.ptp(vtg) > 0 and np.ptp(vbg) > 0, "one gate is frozen — not a paired n-line"
64	
65	# 4. Temperature stayed at base across the fan (a 30 h run spans fridge
66	#    events). Column name varies by era: 'T' (20260124-era RPL_19 has probe
67	#    + fridge both named T — col() takes the first), T_probe/T_fridge later.
68	for tname in ("T_probe", "T"):
69	    if tname in run.cols:
70	        T = run.col(tname)
71	        print(f"{tname}: {np.nanmin(T)*1e3:.0f}–{np.nanmax(T)*1e3:.0f} mK")
72	        break
73	
74	# 5. Lock-ins not flat/NaN (same as gatemap). Gate-current columns are
75	#    usually ABSENT in fan data (plot-only, step 6) — skip, don't fail.
76	for name in set(run.cols):
77	    if name.startswith("sr830_") and name.endswith("_X"):
78	        x = run.col(name)
79	        if np.allclose(x, x[0]) or np.isnan(x).any():
80	            print(f"⚠️  {name} flat or NaN — check sensitivity/wiring")
81	```
82	
83	**Středa read** (the point of the fan): track ρxx dip positions n_dip(B) per B-row and fit dn/dB per dip family.
84	- A linearly dispersing dip is a gapped state with Chern number `C = (h/e) · dn/dB` (n in absolute units). The corpus tools are inline in the ana notebooks: `streda()` returning `B = phi0 * n / C` (RPL_19/20251220_ana cells 96–98) and the overlay form `x_fit = C * y_fit * 1E-16 / (h/e)` plotted over the file-1840 fan (20260124_ana cell 93, C = 1 dashed line with the constants from the boilerplate cell 3).
85	- **Moiré devices**: the slope converts to a Chern number only through the moiré density — `C = (h/e) · n_M · dν_h/dB`. The corpus has no ν_h layer; anchoring n_M and the ν_h↔n conversion is `cap-ratio-calibration`'s job (deferred — recipe not yet written). Until it exists, report slopes in raw dn/dB and flag the assignment.
86	- **Do not hard-code "plateau value ⇒ Středa slope"** [flagged for expert review]: the RIQAH states in arXiv 2504.06972 show ρxy quantized at h/e² while their ρxx dips disperse with slopes near their *fractional filling*, not C = 1 — explicitly unexplained in that paper. A plateau/dispersion mismatch is an escalate-to-expert finding, not a fit error.
87	- **Fan onset as a quality metric**: the lowest B at which oscillations/LL dips resolve tracks quantum mobility — RPL_10's fans resolved structure below 1 T; RPL_19's oscillation check needed 0.9–2.5 T. A later cooldown whose onset field moves up is a device-quality regression worth noting.
88	
89	## Examples
90	- `aaron/RPL_10/241230_measure.ipynb` cells 50–53 — the original fans, exemplary comment discipline. **Cell-range adjustment vs. index**: the index synopsis lumps these under "n-vs-B sweeps at D = 0.31" (cells 49–53); within that, cell 51 is a strict 1D field sweep (claimed by `field-sweep-1d` Examples, which already flags 50/52/53 as "landau-fan-shaped") and cell 54 is a *raw, never-executed* draft fan at D = 0.25. The executed fans: cell 50 → file 156 (101 B × 101 n, B 1→0 T, `slow_delay=30, fast_delay=1`, 4.3 h), cell 52 → file 158 (351 × 201 — **interrupted at 0.0 h** and immediately superseded), cell 53 → file 159 (351 × 251, 27.8 h, the fan the qo-discovery fixture freezes on). Note B runs *downward* (1→0): the magnet was parked at 1 T by the preceding `## Gate maps in field` cells 46–48, so the fan starts where the magnet sits.
91	- `aaron/RPL_19/20260124_measure.ipynb` cells 117–119, 173–176, 234–242, 278–284 — the mature fan family. **Cell-range adjustment vs. index**: the brief cited the "Small fan to check if oscillations are real" as ~cells 167–176; actually 167–172 are still `# Resuming effective mass` (higher field range), the small-fan section is header 173, base-recool cell 174 (`heater.volt(0)` + 1 h `interruptible_sleep`), fans 175 (D = 0.2) and 176 (D = 1) — 161 B steps 0.9→2.5 T × 151-pt n-line, `fast_delay=0.6` → file 1776, 5.5 h, the `after-qo-confirmed` fixture cut. Cells 234–242 are the deep fan (cell 236 → file 1840: 441 × 231, 0.6→5 T, 30.1 h) plus the `## Elevated T Fan` (heater at 2.75 V, 20-min settle, designer hstack n-vector, ±5 T in four chained segments). Cells 123–125 (`# Fan at D = 0.2, valence side` — range as index): cell 124 sets sensitivity *and* `time_constant(300e-3)`, cell 125 sweeps the valence side (n = −3.0→0.0, 201 pts) with `field_vec = np.hstack((np.linspace(0.3, 1.5, 121), np.linspace(1.5, 8, 131)))` — 10 mT steps where structure is fine, 50 mT above.

# Landau fan

## What
2D map of carrier density × magnetic field at fixed displacement field: `mag.field` as the **slow** axis of a `multimegasweep`, with a paired-(k_tg, k_bg) n-line (fixed D, via `calculate_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, dtg=..., dbg=...)`) as the **fast** axis:
```python
s.multimegasweep([mag.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=1, fast_delay=0.9)
```
Field is slow because gates are cheap to retrace and the magnet is not — the magnet ramps once, monotonically, across the whole fan. Every lock-in X/P read at each grid point. Analysis side plots B vs n (`pcolormesh`) per contact pair and overlays Středa lines (see Verify). Distinct from its two neighbors: `field-sweep-1d` is one gate point with full B-axis density; `gatemap-in-field` is the full 2D gate plane at a *single* B. The fan trades both for the (n, B) plane — the only measurement that resolves how gapped states *disperse* with field.

## When
Three triggers, in rough campaign order:
- **Oscillation check** — a `field-sweep-1d` or `gatemap-in-field` showed quantum-oscillation-like wiggles and you need to know if they're real. The corpus idiom is literally named for this: RPL_19's "Small fan to check if oscillations are real" (a 161 × 151 fan after an effective-mass series kept hinting at SdH). A feature that moves systematically across the n-line as B steps is physics; one that doesn't is noise or gate drift.
- **State classification** — a map shows a vanishing-ρxx region (or a busy set of dips) and the discriminating question is whether the features disperse. This is the classification backbone of an FQAH/SC-style campaign (arXiv 2504.06972: ρxx(ν_h, B) fans + Středa fits are how (R/F/I)QAH states were separated from the SC region).
- **Calibration** — SdH/LL frequency vs n gives cap ratios independently of the CNP-slope method, and for a moiré device the fan anchors the moiré density n_M. The extraction is `cap-ratio-calibration`'s job (deferred — recipe not yet written); the fan is its input data.

Prerequisites are `nD-map`'s plus a field-verified magnet: cap ratios `dtg`/`dbg` must be trusted (the fast axis is a line in (n, D) — wrong caps tilt it), and the field source must be live (Yokogawa cache seeded after kernel restart, AMI430 in operating mode — see `field-sweep-1d` plumbing notes).

## Why
A dip in ρxx at one B value is ambiguous — gap, SC, contact artifact, density wobble. The same dip tracked across a fan is nearly unambiguous: a gapped state at fixed filling traces a straight line in (n, B) whose slope *is* its Chern number (Středa: dn/dB = C·e/h), an SC pocket sits at fixed n and dies at moderate B without dispersing, and quantum oscillations fan out with 1/B periodicity that yields the Fermi-surface area. One measurement, three discriminations, plus calibration for free.

The cost is real: these are the most expensive sweeps in the corpus. Reference wall-clocks *(our-measurement, toploader, non-blocking-magnet era — the formula below them omits the traverse term; do not carry these numbers to another rig untagged)*: RPL_10's 101 B × 101 n fan at `slow_delay=30, fast_delay=1` took **4.3 h** (file 156); the 351 × 251 version took **27.8 h** (file 159); RPL_19's 161 × 151 at `fast_delay=0.6` took **5.5 h** (file 1776 — Aaron's own `# 1776, took 5.5 hours` annotation propagates through later fan cells); the 441 × 231 fan to 5 T took **30.1 h** (file 1840). Aaron's inline arithmetic (`(351*501)/(201*151)*3` in 20260124 cell 134) is the toploader-era form.

**Estimate before you run — the full cost model**: wall-clock = **field-traverse time + N_rows × (row turnaround + N_fast × per-point time)**. Which term dominates is a rig property, not a constant of nature: **if the field source is ramp-rate-limited and the set call blocks** (check the rig card for whether yours is), the traverse term is fixed by the B-span alone — **finer B steps cost only row turnaround, and coarsening B buys aliasing, not time**. Traverses come in two species, priced differently: a **bare ramp** moves at the magnet's ramp rate; a **measured traverse** (the same leg recorded as a sweep) moves at an effective rate degraded by per-point overhead. A "free" measured ramp-down is usually still worth taking — it buys data for wall-clock — but it is not free: price it at the measured rate, from the rig card's Timing rules (`rig_card.md`), never the bare one. Calibrate row turnaround and per-point time from this session's own first sweeps; inherited timing constants carry a provenance tag and the conditions they were measured under, or they are guesses.

## Recipe
1. Pick the n-window and fixed D from the map that motivated the fan, and decide the B span. Corpus shapes: oscillation check 0.9 → 2.5 T over a 151-pt n-line; classification fan 0 → 2.5 T, 251 × 151; deep fan 0.6 → 5 T, 441 × 231; high-field 5 → 12 T, 351 × 201. Start coarse (≤200 B steps, ≤151 n points); zoom only on confirmed structure. **Grid Nyquist check, both axes, at design time**: against the finest expected feature spacing in the analysis window. The **B-axis** check depends on the read: a **Středa/SC fan** (dip positions, no FFT) samples uniform in B, may start at 0, and needs ≥2 (prefer 3) rows per LL period ΔB ≈ (g·e/h)·B²/n (g = 4 for spin×valley) at the **lowest-B, highest-n corner**; a **per-column SdH-FFT fan** samples uniform in 1/B (`field_invB`, B_lo > 0) and needs Δ(1/B) ≤ 1/(2·F) (prefer 1/3) at the highest n, F = (h/4e)·n. The **n-axis** check (both): ray spacing Δn = g·(e/h)·B at the lowest B you intend to read, same ≥2 floor. For a **per-column SdH-FFT fan** also compute the resolution **δF = 1/(1/B_onset − 1/B_max)** against the tones the claim must separate (~2·δF to trust a split) — δF is set by the record above onset, not by grid density; if it can't separate the tones, redesign the window or the density, don't densify. An undersampled axis produces in-data aliasing that mimics curved structure and survives re-plotting; no post-hoc check fully recovers it. "Start coarse" applies to the *window*, never below the Nyquist floor of the structure you intend to claim — and where the cost model says fine B is nearly free (blocking ramp-limited magnets), take it. **Re-run this check whenever n_max changes — never inherit the field sampling across fans.** The requirement tightens with n (Δ(1/B) ∝ 1/n, ΔB ∝ B²/n), so a sampling fine enough for an n≤4 fan undersamples an n=10 firming fan (our-measurement, QC0426/VTI 2026-06-14, uniform-B at ΔB=0.1 T: 2.2 rows/period at n=4 but only 1.5 — under the ≥2 floor — at n=10, B=4 T, where a spurious high-n second pocket appeared and had to be killed post-hoc). Where the rig makes fine B *not* free (measurement-dominated fans, e.g. a non-blocking-magnet rig at >1 s/pt — check the cost model), buy the high-n Nyquist floor by **trimming n-points or flooring the high-n claim at B ≥ 5–6 T**, not by coarsening the field sampling. **Dynamic-range check, at design time**: a fan reads through one *fixed* sensitivity, so the scale must clear the **global worst corner**, structurally **low n × high B** — R ∝ 1/n on the gate axis stacks with the B-axis MR (10–100× zero-field). Size full-scale with **headroom, not precision** — saturation is the asymmetric failure: **better to lose low-resistance resolution than saturate** (expert practice). Set the scale comfortably above I_bias·R(n_min, B_max), anchoring R_max from a spot-check/CNP R-anchor × the **low-n** MR factor (MR grows toward CNP; a high-|n| factor under-sizes the corner — our-measurement). **Clipping distorts, it does not drop**: a railed column is flat-topped → harmonics + corrupted bg-subtraction across its whole FFT, unrecoverable by any B-window (the clean data sits at low B, the clip at high B). **Cost-floor check, at design time**: propose **exactly one** fan — the cheapest that clears the two checks above and delivers the claim. Compute `N_B · N_n · t_pt` and set each lever to its floor. **Do not offer a cheaper alternative or defer the trim to the operator — the floored design *is* the proposal.** Levers, in order: (1) **`B_lo` = the measured onset from `hera.analysis.sdh_onset(R, B).onset_b` — compute it, do not eyeball it** (sub-onset rows are background, not signal; a too-low `B_lo` inflates both the 1/B span and the n-axis Nyquist, and eyeballed onsets run systematically too low). If the carrying tone is `censored`, the spot-check record never captured the onset — `onset_b` is that record's low edge, a valid lower bound for `B_lo`; a cheap low-field extension pins it before committing a long fan. `SdhOnsetError` means no usable oscillations — re-examine the spot check, do not guess a `B_lo`; (2) **`n_max` = the validity window of the claim**; (3) `N_n` = its ray-Nyquist floor at `B_lo`; (4) `B_max` = the claim (more periods sharpen tones, but `B_max` past what the claim needs is just cost). `n_max` is the most expensive lever — out-of-validity it pays on *both* `N_B` and `N_n` (`Δ(1/B) ∝ 1/n_max`). State the computed `N_B`, `N_n`, and wall-clock in the proposal.
2. Build the fast axis: `ns = np.linspace(n_hi, n_lo, N); Ds = D0 * np.ones(len(ns)); Vtgs, Vbgs = calculate_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, dtg=..., dbg=...)`. A non-uniform n-vector is legitimate when you know where the action is — RPL_19's elevated-T fan stitches `np.hstack((n1, n2, n3))` with the dense segment over the CSC window and coarse segments elsewhere, with `#`-comments labeling each segment (20260124 cell 239).
3. Set the sensitivity (from the step-1 dynamic-range check) and time constant as an explicit pre-cell, fixed for the whole fan. RPL_19/20260217 cell 124 is the idiom: `sr830_N.sensitivity(10e-3)`, `sr830_N.time_constant(300e-3)`. Excitation: Aaron runs 1 V (graphene-scale) and bumps to 2.5 V for 12 T work; on a fragile-state device (FQAH/SC, arXiv 2504.06972's 1 nA cap) respect the device-card excitation ceiling instead — the states you're classifying wash out if heated.
4. Build the slow field axis: a **per-column SdH-FFT fan** uses `B_vec = field_invB(B_start, B_end, N)` (uniform in 1/B, both > 0); a **Středa/SC fan** uses `np.linspace` and may start at 0. Position the magnet at the fan's start field and let it settle: `s.ramp(mag.field, B_start)` then `time.sleep(600)` for multi-tesla positioning (RPL_19/20260217 cells 88/94), `time.sleep(30)` at ~1 T (RPL_10), `time.sleep(5*60)` at 0.6 T (20260124 cell 235). Plan the direction (endpoint order) so the fan *starts* where the magnet already is and *ends* where the next measurement needs it — never re-traverse. The elevated-T fan covers ±5 T as four chained segments (5→0.6, 0.6→0, 0→−0.6, −0.6→−5; 20260124 cells 239–242), each starting where the last ended.
5. Build `s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)`. `s.add_comment('landau-fan')` then a structured tag: `s.add_comment(f'D = {D0} V/nm, n = {n_lo} to {n_hi}, B = {B_start} to {B_end} T')`, plus `s.add_comment(grab_metadata())` where available. **Watch out** — RPL_10's fans carry exemplary comments (`'MC4, Vsi = -20V, quantum oscillations, D = 0.31 V/nm, n = -2.9 to -2.1, B = 1 to 0 T'`); RPL_19's fan cells carry *none* (files 1776/1840 have empty `comments`) — only a stale `# 1776` Python comment. The recipe asks for the RPL_10 discipline.
6. `s.ramp(sr830_1.amplitude, A)`, `s.ramp(k_si.volt, V_si)`, `s.ramp(bias_voltage.volt, 0)` if present. `fp` temperature(s) and every lock-in X/P; `plot` gate currents for live leakage (`s.plot(k_bg.volt, k_bg.curr)`, `s.plot('time', k_tg.curr)`, `s.plot('time', k_si.curr)` — RPL_19 fan idiom; note `fp` of gate currents is often omitted here, so leakage lands in the live plot but *not* in the TSV).
7. The sweep (step 0 call above). Delay band in the corpus: `slow_delay=1` (gates retrace during it; the field step itself is rate-limited by the magnet), `fast_delay` ≈ 4τ default — a Středa/dispersion fan tolerates the uniform fast-axis lag like a slope; ~6τ when the n-axis carries the extracted signal (per-column SdH FFT, or coarse n), where the lag distorts it, with denser n trading against the dwell.
8. Park gates (`k_bg.volt(0); k_tg.volt(0)`), decide the field endpoint deliberately (leave it for a follow-up fan, `s.ramp(mag.field, 0)`, or ride home as a measured traverse — a free `field-sweep-1d`, priced at the measured rate per the Why cost model), and ping (`alerts.discord('🐍jobs done🐍')`) — at 5–30 h these runs outlive operator attention spans.

## Verify
Disk-side checks, then the Středa read. The fan is unrolled into flat rows; the slow column is `magnet_field`.

```python
from hera.analysis import open_run, plot_raw, summarize_run
import numpy as np

run = open_run("<notebook_dir>/data/<file_id>")
print(summarize_run(run))
# expect: type 2D, recipe 'landau-fan', slow_param ['magnet_field'],
#         fast_param ['k_tg_volt', 'k_bg_volt'].

# 0. Raw view FIRST — one gain-divided pcolormesh per channel, no log, no
#    background removal. Rails/clipping, dead channels, streaks, and row
#    jumps are visible here and hidden by every derived (FFT/Středa) view.
plot_raw(run)

# 1. Completeness — at 5-30 h these are the most interruption-prone sweeps
#    in the corpus (RPL_10 file 158 and TD48-era runs died early; Aaron
#    re-ran rather than salvaged).
assert not run.interrupted, "fan was interrupted; decide re-run vs salvage with the human"

# 2. B axis actually traversed the plan, monotonically per segment.
B = run.col("magnet_field")
print(f"B traversed: {B.min():.3f} → {B.max():.3f} T over {len(run.meta['slow_setpoints'][0])} steps")

# 3. Fast axis is a paired n-line: both gate columns move together.
vtg, vbg = run.col("k_tg_volt"), run.col("k_bg_volt")
assert np.ptp(vtg) > 0 and np.ptp(vbg) > 0, "one gate is frozen — not a paired n-line"

# 4. Temperature stayed at base across the fan (a 30 h run spans fridge
#    events). Column name varies by era: 'T' (20260124-era RPL_19 has probe
#    + fridge both named T — col() takes the first), T_probe/T_fridge later.
for tname in ("T_probe", "T"):
    if tname in run.cols:
        T = run.col(tname)
        print(f"{tname}: {np.nanmin(T)*1e3:.0f}–{np.nanmax(T)*1e3:.0f} mK")
        break

# 5. Lock-ins not flat/NaN (same as gatemap). Gate-current columns are
#    usually ABSENT in fan data (plot-only, step 6) — skip, don't fail.
for name in set(run.cols):
    if name.startswith("sr830_") and name.endswith("_X"):
        x = run.col(name)
        if np.allclose(x, x[0]) or np.isnan(x).any():
            print(f"⚠️  {name} flat or NaN — check sensitivity/wiring")
```

**Středa read** (the point of the fan): track ρxx dip positions n_dip(B) per B-row and fit dn/dB per dip family.
- A linearly dispersing dip is a gapped state with Chern number `C = (h/e) · dn/dB` (n in absolute units). The corpus tools are inline in the ana notebooks: `streda()` returning `B = phi0 * n / C` (RPL_19/20251220_ana cells 96–98) and the overlay form `x_fit = C * y_fit * 1E-16 / (h/e)` plotted over the file-1840 fan (20260124_ana cell 93, C = 1 dashed line with the constants from the boilerplate cell 3).
- **Moiré devices**: the slope converts to a Chern number only through the moiré density — `C = (h/e) · n_M · dν_h/dB`. The corpus has no ν_h layer; anchoring n_M and the ν_h↔n conversion is `cap-ratio-calibration`'s job (deferred — recipe not yet written). Until it exists, report slopes in raw dn/dB and flag the assignment.
- **Do not hard-code "plateau value ⇒ Středa slope"** [flagged for expert review]: the RIQAH states in arXiv 2504.06972 show ρxy quantized at h/e² while their ρxx dips disperse with slopes near their *fractional filling*, not C = 1 — explicitly unexplained in that paper. A plateau/dispersion mismatch is an escalate-to-expert finding, not a fit error.
- **Fan onset as a quality metric**: the lowest B at which oscillations/LL dips resolve tracks quantum mobility — RPL_10's fans resolved structure below 1 T; RPL_19's oscillation check needed 0.9–2.5 T. A later cooldown whose onset field moves up is a device-quality regression worth noting.

## Examples
- `aaron/RPL_10/241230_measure.ipynb` cells 50–53 — the original fans, exemplary comment discipline. **Cell-range adjustment vs. index**: the index synopsis lumps these under "n-vs-B sweeps at D = 0.31" (cells 49–53); within that, cell 51 is a strict 1D field sweep (claimed by `field-sweep-1d` Examples, which already flags 50/52/53 as "landau-fan-shaped") and cell 54 is a *raw, never-executed* draft fan at D = 0.25. The executed fans: cell 50 → file 156 (101 B × 101 n, B 1→0 T, `slow_delay=30, fast_delay=1`, 4.3 h), cell 52 → file 158 (351 × 201 — **interrupted at 0.0 h** and immediately superseded), cell 53 → file 159 (351 × 251, 27.8 h, the fan the qo-discovery fixture freezes on). Note B runs *downward* (1→0): the magnet was parked at 1 T by the preceding `## Gate maps in field` cells 46–48, so the fan starts where the magnet sits.
- `aaron/RPL_19/20260124_measure.ipynb` cells 117–119, 173–176, 234–242, 278–284 — the mature fan family. **Cell-range adjustment vs. index**: the brief cited the "Small fan to check if oscillations are real" as ~cells 167–176; actually 167–172 are still `# Resuming effective mass` (higher field range), the small-fan section is header 173, base-recool cell 174 (`heater.volt(0)` + 1 h `interruptible_sleep`), fans 175 (D = 0.2) and 176 (D = 1) — 161 B steps 0.9→2.5 T × 151-pt n-line, `fast_delay=0.6` → file 1776, 5.5 h, the `after-qo-confirmed` fixture cut. Cell 119 is the first `## Test fan` (501 × 51, B 0.75–1.25 T at 1 mT steps). Cells 234–242 are the deep fan (cell 236 → file 1840: 441 × 231, 0.6→5 T, 30.1 h) plus the `## Elevated T Fan` (heater at 2.75 V, 20-min settle, designer hstack n-vector, ±5 T in four chained segments). Cells 280–283 (`# Landau fans`) repeat a 251 × 151 shape across D = 1.04/0.95/0.9/0.25 — a D-ladder of fans, each cell differing only in `ns`/`Ds` and sweep direction (alternating 2.5→0 / 0→2.5 so consecutive fans never re-traverse). No `add_comment` in any of these — see Recipe step 5.
- `aaron/RPL_19/20260217_measure.ipynb` cells 87–96 and 123–126 — fans with explicit field-settle and lock-in-setup cells. Cells 88/91/94 are `s.ramp(mag.field, B); time.sleep(600)` positioning cells; cell 89 presets sensitivity; cells 90/92 are 201 × 101 CSC fans at D = 1.02/0.98 (2.5→0.5 T); cell 95 is the 12 T fan (5→12 T, 351 × 201); cell 96 descends 12→0 with the two-density hstack `field_vec`. Cells 123–125 (`# Fan at D = 0.2, valence side` — range as index): cell 124 sets sensitivity *and* `time_constant(300e-3)`, cell 125 sweeps the valence side (n = −3.0→0.0, 201 pts) with `field_vec = np.hstack((np.linspace(0.3, 1.5, 121), np.linspace(1.5, 8, 131)))` — 10 mT steps where structure is fine, 50 mT above.

## Next
- **Oscillations confirmed real**: two branches, both exercised in RPL_19/20260124 — (a) `field-sweep-1d` cuts at fixed (n, D) with high B-density to read the SdH frequency cleanly (`# Cuts at fixed n and D`, cell 177 — the `after-qo-confirmed` fixture's contested decision), and (b) an effective-mass temperature series: repeat one field sweep at a heater ladder and fit amplitude vs T — that is `temperature-dependence` Flavor B.
- **Dips disperse linearly**: (F/I)QAH-family candidate with C from the slope. Cross-check the Hall channel for the matching plateau; if plateau and slope disagree, escalate (RIQAH caution above). Assigning ν requires n_M — `cap-ratio-calibration` (deferred).
- **A vanishing-ρxx region does NOT disperse and dies at moderate B**: SC candidate. Next: `field-sweep-1d` fine B-scans at the region's center (critical field, ±mT hygiene), `hysteresis-check` for switching, and dV/dI vs I_dc when `bias-spectroscopy` exists (deferred) — cf. arXiv 2504.06972's SC dome (B_c ≈ 0.6–0.8 T).
- **Fan looks streaky / row-to-row jumps**: sensitivity changed mid-fan (autorange left on) or the magnet didn't settle. Re-run with the step-3 preset cell and a longer step-4 settle.
- **Low-n columns flat-topped / high-B FFT is junk**: fixed sensitivity under-ranged the low-n × high-B corner — *clipping*, distinct from the autorange streak above. Not salvageable by windowing (clipping lives at high B, where the SdH signal is strongest). Re-run with the step-1 worst-corner sizing.
- **Caps or n_M wanted from this fan**: `cap-ratio-calibration` (deferred) — the SdH-frequency method; until written, the extraction is ana-side judgment (cf. the QO FFT pipeline, RPL_19/20260112_ana cell 125).
- **Fan at one D is interesting**: D-ladder of fans (20260124 cells 280–283 idiom) or an `Elevated T Fan` to see which features survive warming — `temperature-dependence` decides the ladder.

39	settle), which makes a multi-tesla fan **measurement-dominated** — the bare
40	traverse (~1 h at 8 T) is small against the grid. So the base's
41	*measurement-dominated* branch applies: buy the high-n Nyquist floor (base
42	step 1, the n_max re-check) by **trimming n-points or flooring the high-n
43	claim**, never by adding B rows blindly. "Fine B is nearly free" is a
44	toploader-era (non-blocking-magnet, traverse-dominated) statement; do not
45	carry it to this rig.
46	
47	## Examples
48	
49	- A VTI trilayer fan *(our-measurement, 2026-06-14)*: `file_id 20`, D = 0,
50	  0 → 8 T paired n-line, `magnet.field` slow axis, ~1.44 s/pt at a 4τ dwell —
51	  the measurement-dominated regime above (8 T bare traverse ≈ 1 h ≪ grid
52	  time). The firming fan `file_id 21` rode the magnet home (8 → 0 T) as a
53	  measured ramp-down, picking up high-n rows on the way — the base's

# Landau fan — VTI variant

**Base**: `measurements/landau-fan.md`. This file carries only the deltas
(STYLE rule 13); read the base first. Runs executed under this variant tag
`s.add_comment('landau-fan-vti')`.

The base's Recipe steps are toploader-flavored in their call surface (driver
names, an explicit field-settle sleep, a Discord ping). On the VTI those
names and the settle discipline differ; the *method* — coarse-first design,
both-axis Nyquist, Středa read — is unchanged.

**Overridden steps and the rig facts that force them:**

- **Steps 0/5, field parameter** — the field parameter is
  **`magnet.field`** (the instrument instance is named `magnet`, not `mag`);
  the station builder is `sweep.AsyncStation(mc)`, same as the base. The
  slow-axis call is
  `s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=…, fast_delay=…)`.
- **Step 2, fast axis** — the gate-voltage helper is
  `sharpelab_nb.gates.calc_gate_voltages(n, D, c_tg, c_bg, n_offset, D_offset)`
  (the `(c_tg, c_bg, offsets)` form written back by
  `cnp-and-dline-calibration`), not `calculate_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, dtg=, dbg=)`.
- **Step 4, field positioning** — `magnet.field(target)` **blocks until the
  field is reached** (FastBi1K5 blocking ramp; see the rig card's magnet
  Set-semantics). So there is **no `time.sleep(600)` pre-settle** — the set
  call *is* the settle. Position by `magnet.field(B_start)` and proceed.
- **Step 8, notify** — `hera-notify` on the operator's key (rig notify
  channel), not `alerts.discord`.
- **Step 6, fp list** — follow the rig card's instrument-polling rules when
  building the `fp` set; the card names which instruments are unsafe to poll
  per-point on this rig. *(The base says "fp temperature(s)"; the card
  governs — do not restate the hazard here.)*

**Cost-model regime (base Why).** The base's "finer B steps cost only row
turnaround, and coarsening B buys aliasing, not time" corollary holds only
when the grid is cheap relative to the traverse. On the VTI the magnet is
blocking-ramp-limited (so the traverse term is fixed by the B-span) **but
per-point time is ~1.2–1.4 s/pt** (rig card Timing; ~1.44 s/pt at a 4τ
settle), which makes a multi-tesla fan **measurement-dominated** — the bare
traverse (~1 h at 8 T) is small against the grid. So the base's
*measurement-dominated* branch applies: buy the high-n Nyquist floor (base
step 1, the n_max re-check) by **trimming n-points or flooring the high-n
claim**, never by adding B rows blindly. "Fine B is nearly free" is a
toploader-era (non-blocking-magnet, traverse-dominated) statement; do not
carry it to this rig.

## Examples

- A VTI trilayer fan *(our-measurement, 2026-06-14)*: `file_id 20`, D = 0,
  0 → 8 T paired n-line, `magnet.field` slow axis, ~1.44 s/pt at a 4τ dwell —
  the measurement-dominated regime above (8 T bare traverse ≈ 1 h ≪ grid
  time). The firming fan `file_id 21` rode the magnet home (8 → 0 T) as a
  measured ramp-down, picking up high-n rows on the way — the base's
  "plan the direction so the fan ends where the next measurement needs it".

## Next

Base `## Next` applies unchanged.

## Obsolescence

Delete this file when the base recipe goes fully instrument-class-conditional
(driver names — `magnet.field`, the notify channel — move
to the rig card, leaving the base name-free): the cost-regime note then folds
into the base's rig-property cost discussion, and the settle/fast-axis deltas
become base conditionals the rig card resolves. Moving fans onto a continuous
on-the-fly ramp (the driver's `start_field_ramp` + sampled readback, outside
the blocking `sweep` set) would also retire the step-4 delta.
